summary: The audit checks the 135 units of graduate work, all in courses numbered 100 or above. Checked by hand: aligning with an advisor by your third quarter, 21 units of approved 200-level engineering, science and math courses beyond the MS, breadth (a minor or 9 approved units outside your research topic), the program proposal, the reading committee, the Green Light meeting, the qualifying exam, candidacy, teaching, the 3.0 GPA, the oral exam and the dissertation. Up to 45 units from an MS elsewhere may transfer with approval.

totals.label: Courses numbered below 100
totals.why: "PhD candidates must complete a minimum of 135 units. These courses must be numbered 100+."

w8DMES8Y.why: "Aligning with an advisor is an essential milestone in the PhD program" "PhD students who do not align with an advisor by the 3rd quarter of study at Stanford are subject to dismissal". "PhD candidates must complete a minimum of 135 units. These courses must be numbered 100+." "a student must complete a minimum of 21 units of approved courses in advanced study in engineering, science, and mathematics (excluding research, directed study, seminars, curricular practical training, and course) beyond the MS degree. These courses must be numbered 200+, be taken for a letter grade, and have primarily technical content." "the department has a breadth requirement for the PhD degree. This may be satisfied by a formal minor in another department (generally 20 units) or by at least nine units of coursework (outside of the primary research topic) which the principal dissertation advisor approves." "PhD students are required to file a preliminary PhD program proposal" "After attaining PhD Candidacy, the student must form a Reading Committee" "No less than six months before the planned PhD Oral Exam, the student and the Reading Committee are required to meet in a 'Green Light Meeting.'" The fields name no subject codes, so the courses are moved in by the student.
